description: A small, fast-growing tree with edible flowers and leaves, heavily used in Ayurveda and culinary practices.
medical_uses: Treats night blindness, headaches, catarrh, and fevers. Highly rich in Vitamin A and calcium.
treatment_methods: Consume the flowers and leaves cooked as a vegetable or steep the bark for a medicinal decoction.
care_instructions: Thrives in full sun and well-draining soil. Requires regular watering and a tropical climate.

description: A large evergreen tree with leaves in whorls of seven, known as the 'Devil's Tree' in some cultures.
medical_uses: Used traditionally for malaria, chronic diarrhea, dysentery, and to improve bowel tone.
treatment_methods: The bark is boiled to make an astringent decoction. Dosage must be controlled as high doses can be toxic.
care_instructions: Needs tropical conditions, full sun to partial shade, and moist, well-draining soil.

description: A beautiful ornamental tree known for its cascading racemes of bright yellow flowers.
medical_uses: A safe and effective purgative. Treats constipation, skin disorders, and fever.
treatment_methods: The fruit pulp is soaked in water and consumed as a gentle laxative.
care_instructions: Requires full sun and well-draining soil. Very drought-tolerant once established.

description: A perennial herb resembling chamomile, recognized by its roots which cause a tingling sensation on the tongue.
medical_uses: Treats toothache, sore throat, and delayed speech in children. Acts as a nerve stimulant.
treatment_methods: Chew a small piece of the root for instant toothache relief or use powdered root in honey.
care_instructions: Prefers well-drained sandy or loamy soil and full sun. Needs moderate watering.

description: A deciduous tree known for its spectacular bright orange-red flowers that bloom in spring.
medical_uses: Treats bleeding disorders, intestinal worms, and skin diseases.
treatment_methods: Seeds are used as an anthelmintic (dewormer). Flowers are steeped to make a cooling drink.
care_instructions: Drought-resistant, grows in poor soil, and requires full sunlight.

description: A perennial winter-deciduous plant that bears rounded, fleshy leaves and large white to pinkish-white flowers.
medical_uses: Protects the liver, treats rheumatism, and acts as a diuretic and expectorant.
treatment_methods: The unopened flower buds (capers) and roots are used in dietary and medicinal preparations.
care_instructions: Requires dry heat and intense sunlight. Thrives in poor, rocky, and well-draining soils.

description: A perennial succulent vine characterized by its quadrangular stems, often used to heal bone fractures.
medical_uses: Accelerates bone healing, treats osteoporosis, and relieves joint pain.
treatment_methods: The stem juice is consumed or applied topically over fractures alongside traditional splinting.
care_instructions: Thrives in warm, dry climates. Needs well-draining soil and can tolerate prolonged droughts.

description: A vigorous twining vine bearing striking, deep blue flowers with a light yellow center.
medical_uses: Acts as a brain tonic. Improves memory, reduces stress, and treats neurological disorders.
treatment_methods: The roots and seeds are powdered and consumed, or flowers are brewed into a calming blue tea.
care_instructions: Prefers full sun and rich, moist, well-draining soil. Requires a trellis for support.

description: A tall perennial herb with large, spirally arranged leaves and beautiful white flowers with a red center.
medical_uses: Treats diabetes, fever, asthma, and bronchitis.
treatment_methods: The rhizome is boiled into a decoction or crushed to extract juice for respiratory and metabolic disorders.
care_instructions: Needs partial shade and moist, well-draining soil. Frost-sensitive.

description: A wild-growing herbaceous annual with trumpet-shaped flowers and spiky fruit capsules. Highly toxic.
medical_uses: Used externally for severe joint pain, asthma (in controlled ancient practices), and muscle spasms.
treatment_methods: Strictly for external use. Leaves are warmed and tied over painful joints to relieve arthritis.
care_instructions: Grows vigorously in disturbed soils and full sun. Must be kept away from children and pets due to extreme toxicity.

description: A pantropical weed characterized by hairy stems and a milky sap that exudes when broken.
medical_uses: Treats respiratory issues like asthma, bronchitis, and gastrointestinal disorders.
treatment_methods: The entire plant is boiled into a tea for asthma or the sap is applied to warts.
care_instructions: A hardy weed that grows in almost any soil and full sun. Highly drought-tolerant.

description: A delicate, highly branched annual herb with clusters of small pinkish-purple flowers.
medical_uses: Acts as a blood purifier, treats liver disorders, and relieves burning sensations in the body.
treatment_methods: The whole plant is dried and brewed into a bitter decoction for liver and skin health.
care_instructions: A winter weed that prefers cool climates, moist soil, and partial shade.

description: A striking climbing plant with flame-like red and yellow flowers. Highly poisonous if ingested.
medical_uses: Used externally for gout, arthritis, and to stimulate labor in traditional practices.
treatment_methods: Strictly applied topically as a paste over inflamed joints. Never ingested.
care_instructions: Requires a trellis, well-draining soil, and a warm, humid climate.

description: A woody climbing shrub native to the tropical forests of India, Africa, and Australia.
medical_uses: The 'sugar destroyer'. Reduces sugar cravings, lowers blood sugar levels, and aids in weight loss.
treatment_methods: Chew fresh leaves to suppress sweet taste or take powdered dried leaves before meals.
care_instructions: Needs a support structure, partial shade, and well-draining loamy soil.

description: A massive, rampant climbing shrub with highly fragrant, fringed white and yellow flowers.
medical_uses: Treats skin diseases, rheumatism, and asthma.
treatment_methods: The bark and leaves are processed into a paste for topical application or brewed into a mild decoction.
care_instructions: Prefers full sun to partial shade and moist, well-drained soil. Can become invasive if not pruned.

description: A small to medium-sized deciduous tree bearing white, fragrant flowers and long, paired follicles.
medical_uses: The supreme remedy for dysentery, diarrhea, and intestinal parasites.
treatment_methods: The bark and seeds (Indrayava) are powdered and consumed with buttermilk or water.
care_instructions: Grows in dry, deciduous forests. Thrives in full sun and rocky, well-draining soil.

description: A large, much-branched, woody climbing vine with rusty-haired young stems.
medical_uses: Purifies blood, treats skin diseases, and acts as a cooling tonic.
treatment_methods: The roots are boiled to make a cooling and detoxifying decoction.
care_instructions: Requires full sun to partial shade and moist, well-draining soil.

description: A twining shrub with a corky bark and small, greenish-yellow flowers.
medical_uses: Acts as a general restorative tonic. Improves vision and treats tuberculosis.
treatment_methods: The roots and leaves are consumed as a powder or boiled with milk for nourishment.
care_instructions: Drought-resistant. Grows well in sandy, well-draining soil under full sun.

description: A small to medium-sized tree whose fruits are covered in a bright red, glandular powder.
medical_uses: Treats tapeworm infections and skin diseases like scabies and ringworm.
treatment_methods: The red powder from the fruit is taken internally (with caution) for worms or applied externally.
care_instructions: Adaptable to various soils. Prefers full sun and moderate watering.

description: A beautiful evergreen tree known for its heavy, hard wood and large, fragrant white flowers with yellow stamens.
medical_uses: Treats bleeding piles, dysentery, and excessive menstrual bleeding.
treatment_methods: The dried stamens are powdered and consumed with butter or honey.
care_instructions: Requires a humid, tropical climate, partial shade when young, and well-draining, fertile soil.

description: A medium-sized evergreen tree prized for its intensely fragrant, star-shaped cream-colored flowers.
medical_uses: Strengthens teeth and gums, treats headaches, and heals wounds.
treatment_methods: Chew the twigs for oral hygiene. Boil the bark to make an astringent mouthwash.
care_instructions: Prefers coastal and tropical climates. Thrives in full sun and well-draining sandy loam.

description: A medium-sized tree found in the sub-Himalayan region, bearing small, edible, red, berry-like fruits.
medical_uses: Treats asthma, chronic coughs, diarrhea, and fever.
treatment_methods: The bark is powdered and used as a snuff for headaches or taken internally for respiratory issues.
care_instructions: Requires cool, sub-tropical climates and acidic, well-draining soils.

description: An annual flowering plant known for its black seeds, often referred to as 'black cumin'.
medical_uses: Boosts immunity, treats asthma, lowers blood pressure, and promotes hair growth.
treatment_methods: Consume the seeds daily or apply cold-pressed black seed oil to the skin and scalp.
care_instructions: Prefers full sun and rich, well-draining soil. Requires regular watering during the growing season.

description: A small tree that blooms with intensely fragrant white flowers with orange stems, which fall at dawn.
medical_uses: Treats sciatica, arthritis, chronic fevers (like malaria), and acts as a mild laxative.
treatment_methods: Boil the leaves into a strong decoction to relieve sciatic nerve pain and joint inflammation.
care_instructions: Needs a tropical climate, full sun to partial shade, and well-draining soil.

description: A small to medium-sized deciduous tree with massive compound leaves and large, sword-like seed pods.
medical_uses: A key ingredient in 'Dashamoola'. Treats diarrhea, dysentery, joint pain, and asthma.
treatment_methods: The root bark is boiled into a decoction for internal use or applied as a paste on swollen joints.
care_instructions: Thrives in moist, deciduous forests. Prefers full sun and well-drained loamy soil.

description: An erect, annual herb recognized for its tiny, dark brown seeds.
medical_uses: The primary Ayurvedic remedy for vitiligo, psoriasis, and leprosy.
treatment_methods: The seed powder or oil is applied directly to the depigmented skin, followed by brief sun exposure.
care_instructions: Requires full sun, warm temperatures, and well-draining sandy loam. Drought tolerant.

description: A large deciduous tree known as the Indian Kino Tree, whose wood and resin are highly medicinal.
medical_uses: Excellent for managing diabetes, reducing cholesterol, and treating skin diseases.
treatment_methods: Water stored overnight in tumblers made of its wood is consumed in the morning to lower blood sugar.
care_instructions: Requires tropical climates, full sun, and well-draining soil. Can grow very large.

description: A large, thorny, deciduous shrub or small tree bearing round, yellowish fruits.
medical_uses: The premier herb used for inducing vomiting (Vamana therapy) in Panchakarma detoxification.
treatment_methods: The fruit powder is administered with honey and rock salt specifically to induce therapeutic emesis.
care_instructions: Extremely hardy. Grows in dry, deciduous forests in full sun and poor soils.

description: A perennial subshrub with heart-shaped leaves, renowned for its strength-giving properties.
medical_uses: Treats nervous disorders, asthma, weight loss, and builds muscle strength and stamina.
treatment_methods: The root and leaves are boiled with milk or made into medicated massage oils (e.g., Mahanarayan Taila).
care_instructions: Grows wild as a weed. Prefers full sun and well-draining sandy or loamy soils.

description: A climbing, woody vine with prickly stems and tuberous roots.
medical_uses: Treats syphilis, gout, rheumatoid arthritis, and chronic skin diseases.
treatment_methods: The tuberous roots are dried, powdered, and consumed as a decoction or with honey.
care_instructions: Requires partial shade, moist, rich, and well-draining soil, along with a trellis for climbing.

description: A strongly scented, spreading aromatic herb with distinct globose, purple flower heads.
medical_uses: Treats gout, enlarged spleen, skin diseases, and acts as a general nervine tonic.
treatment_methods: The whole plant or the flower heads are dried and consumed as a powder or decoction.
care_instructions: A weed of damp places and paddy fields. Thrives in moist, waterlogged clay soils.

description: A medium-sized tree bearing fruit resembling small oranges, containing highly toxic, disk-shaped seeds.
medical_uses: A powerful nerve stimulant. Treats paralysis, neuralgia, and chronic dyspepsia.
treatment_methods: Extremely toxic. Seeds must undergo rigorous purification (Shodhana) before use in minute, prescribed doses.
care_instructions: Requires a hot, tropical climate. Thrives in full sun and well-draining laterite soils.

description: An annual or biennial herb native to the Himalayas, known for its intense bitterness.
medical_uses: Treats chronic fevers, liver disorders, malaria, and improves appetite.
treatment_methods: The whole plant is soaked in water overnight, and the extremely bitter infusion is consumed the next morning.
care_instructions: Requires cool, high-altitude climates. Plant in moist, well-draining, humus-rich soil.

description: A highly branched, sub-erect herbaceous perennial that grows widely as a wasteland weed.
medical_uses: The best herb for treating an enlarged spleen, liver disorders, and chronic wounds.
treatment_methods: The root is chewed or boiled into a decoction for spleen and liver health.
care_instructions: Grows vigorously in dry, sandy, or rocky soils. Highly drought-tolerant and requires full sun.

description: A climbing, herbaceous vine with heart-shaped leaves, renowned as the 'root of immortality'.
medical_uses: A supreme immunomodulator. Treats dengue, malaria, chronic fevers, diabetes, and arthritis.
treatment_methods: The stem is crushed and boiled to make a potent decoction, often taken with ginger and honey.
care_instructions: Requires a support tree (like Neem for added potency), full sun to partial shade, and moderate watering.

description: An annual plant cultivated worldwide; its seeds and leaves are staples in Indian cooking.
medical_uses: Lowers blood sugar, improves milk production in nursing mothers, and reduces menstrual discomfort.
treatment_methods: Soak seeds overnight and drink the water. Use leaves fresh in cooking or dry for later use.
care_instructions: Requires full sun and well-draining, slightly acidic soil. Cool weather crop.

description: An erect, little-branched perennial herb with distinctive variegated leaves and dense, cylindrical flower spikes.
medical_uses: A key ingredient in 'Dashamoola'. Treats asthma, heart disease, bleeding disorders, and fractures.
treatment_methods: The whole plant, particularly the root, is boiled to make a strengthening decoction.
care_instructions: Prefers tropical climates, well-draining loamy soils, and full sun to partial shade.

description: A perennial herb native to the Himalayas, yielding a highly aromatic rhizome used as a sedative.
medical_uses: Treats insomnia, anxiety, epilepsy, and acts as a potent nervine relaxant.
treatment_methods: The dried root powder is consumed with warm milk before bed or used in aromatherapy.
care_instructions: Requires high altitudes, cool temperatures, partial shade, and moist, rich soil.

description: A much-branched, highly spreading shrub known for its brilliant, tubular red flowers.
medical_uses: Treats severe diarrhea, dysentery, bleeding disorders, and acts as a fermentation agent in Ayurvedic wines (Asavas).
treatment_methods: The dried flowers are powdered and taken with honey, or added to herbal decoctions to initiate fermentation.
care_instructions: Extremely hardy. Thrives in full sun, rocky, well-draining soils, and dry climates.

description: A flowering plant whose rhizome, ginger root, is a universally used spice and folk medicine.
medical_uses: Treats nausea, motion sickness, osteoarthritis, indigestion, and chronic coughs.
treatment_methods: Crush fresh ginger into tea, chew it with salt before meals, or use dried powder (Shunthi) in formulas.
care_instructions: Requires hot, humid climates, partial shade, and rich, consistently moist, well-draining soil.

description: A trailing weed known to 'rejuvenate' the body, featuring small pink flowers and sticky seeds.
medical_uses: A powerful diuretic. Treats kidney disorders, edema (swelling), anemia, and urinary tract infections.
treatment_methods: The whole plant is dried and consumed as a decoction, or the fresh leaves are cooked as a vegetable.
care_instructions: A highly resilient weed. Thrives in full sun and almost any soil type. Needs very little water.

description: A small shrub native to the Arabian Peninsula and India, recognized for its yellow flowers and flat seed pods.
medical_uses: An FDA-approved nonprescription laxative. Used to treat severe constipation and clear the bowel before diagnostic tests.
treatment_methods: The dried leaves or pods are brewed into a tea. Must be used short-term to avoid dependency.
care_instructions: Requires hot, dry climates, full sun, and well-draining sandy soils. Highly drought-tolerant.

description: A small, herbaceous, frost-tender perennial plant that grows creeping along the ground in swampy areas.
medical_uses: The ultimate brain food. Enhances memory, heals wounds, treats varicose veins, and reduces anxiety.
treatment_methods: Eat fresh leaves in salads, extract the juice, or brew dried leaves into a restorative tea.
care_instructions: Needs high moisture and humidity. Grow in partial shade in continuously moist, boggy soil.

description: A small, hairy, perennial herb with beautiful, tiny, sky-blue, funnel-shaped flowers.
medical_uses: A powerful brain tonic. Enhances cognitive function, reduces stress, treats epilepsy, and induces sleep.
treatment_methods: The entire plant is dried, powdered, and consumed with warm milk or made into a medicated syrup.
care_instructions: Grows wild in open, grassy areas. Prefers full sun and well-draining, sandy or rocky soils.

description: A slender, twining, aromatic shrub known for its sweet-smelling roots that resemble the scent of vanilla.
medical_uses: Purifies the blood, treats skin diseases like eczema, acts as a coolant, and manages autoimmune disorders.
treatment_methods: Boil the dried roots to make a fragrant herbal tea or decoction, often consumed during hot summers.
care_instructions: Thrives in partial shade to full sun. Requires well-drained, sandy loam soil. Moderately drought-tolerant.

description: A vigorous climbing legume known for the extreme itchiness caused by the hairs on its seed pods.
medical_uses: A natural source of L-DOPA. Used for Parkinson's disease, nervous disorders, and male infertility.
treatment_methods: The seeds are strictly processed and powdered, typically consumed with milk. Great care must be taken to avoid the irritating pod hairs.
care_instructions: Requires a tropical climate, full sun, and a trellis for support. Plant in well-drained, sandy loam soil.

description: A widespread tropical weed characterized by small, round leaves arranged in rows with tiny fruits hidden underneath.
medical_uses: Highly effective for liver disorders including Hepatitis B, jaundice, and helps break down kidney stones.
treatment_methods: Crush the entire fresh plant to extract juice, or use dried plant powder boiled as a decoction.
care_instructions: Grows easily in tropical environments. Prefers partial shade and moist, well-draining soil.

description: An evergreen shrub with whorled leaves and small, pinkish-white flowers, famous as the source of reserpine.
medical_uses: A powerful tranquilizer used to treat severe high blood pressure, insomnia, and psychiatric disorders.
treatment_methods: The roots are dried and ground. Due to its high potency, it must only be taken under strict medical supervision.
care_instructions: Requires a hot, humid climate. Prefers partial shade and deep, fertile, highly organic, well-draining soil.

description: A prickly, low-growing perennial herb bearing bright purple flowers and yellow berries, covered in spines.
medical_uses: A primary herb for respiratory ailments: treats asthma, chronic coughs, chest pain, and bronchitis.
treatment_methods: The entire plant (roots, leaves, berries) is dried and boiled into a decoction, consumed with honey.
care_instructions: Grows wild in dry, arid waste lands. Thrives in full sun and poor, sandy, well-draining soils.

description: A low-growing, creeping plant with thorny fruits, often considered a weed but highly valued in Ayurveda.
medical_uses: Treats urinary tract infections, kidney stones, improves sexual health, and builds muscle strength.
treatment_methods: The dried fruits and roots are powdered and boiled in water to make a decoction, often taken with honey.
care_instructions: Thrives in dry, sandy, and arid environments. Requires full sunlight and very little water.
